decisions.reason: The candidate already requires ETH and USDC to be selectable wallet currencies, and its same-message failure records the missing ETH option. Card availability is owned by the source Requirement.
The source confirms that ETH should be selectable but does not change the existing requirement that ETH wallet minting is enabled or alter its conversion flow.

The candidate is already deferred to post-launch. Requiring the unimplemented Card option to be non-selectable does not cancel or modify the future Transak integration, and implementation status must not be propagated.
The wallet-provisioning requirement is already deferred with the fiat flow, and temporary Card unavailability does not alter its future provisioning semantics.
The source changes payment-option availability only and does not revise how fiat buyers will access commissions, tickets, prizes, or their provisioned wallets.
Payment-method gating does not change whether tipping is offered, its placement, or its preset and custom amounts.
The source does not change the $15 sale allocation, affiliate commission, founder allocation, prize-pool allocation, or fiat-fee treatment.
USDC remains selectable in the source message, and no change is made to the required USDC mint flow or successful-mint outcome.
The source changes which payment methods may be selected but does not change the $15 primary mint price or its advertised pricing commitment.
The message does not change the condition under which the mint-success modal may appear.
Payment-option gating does not change the NFT ebook product type or unlimited primary-mint supply model.
The payment-method decision does not alter referral-code validity or self-referral prevention rules.
